summary: httpz-requests ships Telegram-controlled remote shell as compiled Cython binaries under a typosquat name
details: Package `httpz-requests` on PyPI presents itself as a 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management' and depends on python-telegram-bot>=20.0. Its `__init__.py` exposes `start_bot`, and all functional code is shipped as compiled Cython.so modules (`bot`, `handlers`, `core`, `obfuscate`) with no accompanying.py sources. The data flow is Telegram messages from a remote operator to command execution on the installing host — a network-controlled shell / backdoor on the installer's machine. Source is deliberately hidden: Cython modules are built with CYTHON_COMPRESS_STRINGS so hardcoded bot tokens, owner/chat IDs, command handlers, and any additional network endpoints are not visible to static review; the package additionally ships a submodule literally named `obfuscate`. The package name typosquats the top PyPI HTTP clients `httpx` and `requests` while the shipped functionality is unrelated to HTTP client work, and publisher metadata is unfilled placeholder text (`Author-email: Aapka Naam <you@example.com>`, `Homepage: github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests`), consistent with a throwaway account. An installer arriving at this package via a typo hands remote shell control of their host to whoever holds the embedded Telegram bot credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
